TIER IV and Shunan target driverless port dump trucks by late 2028

TIER IV and Shunan Bulk Terminal announced a collaboration on November 12 to automate currently crewed dump-truck operations at Japan’s Tokuyama-Kudamatsu port. The first route connects fuel storage with Tokuyama’s power-generation facilities. Driverless operations are targeted by the end of 2028.

TIER IV ↗12 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

Starting with a fuel-haul route

TIER IV and Shunan Bulk Terminal announced a collaboration on November 12 to automate currently crewed dump-truck operations at Japan’s Tokuyama-Kudamatsu port. The first route connects fuel storage with Tokuyama’s power-generation facilities. Driverless operations are targeted by the end of 2028.

Site-specific technology and operations

TIER IV brings Autoware and autonomous-vehicle development and operational experience; the terminal contributes transport expertise. The partners will develop both technology and operating procedures for the site. The truck will use Idemitsu Renewable Diesel, with a parallel aim of reducing transport emissions.

A development project, not a launched service

The release names no truck manufacturer, fleet size, payload or contract value. The 2028 goal does not mean driverless service has begun. The partners will consider nearby routes after gaining experience. For Thai ports and factories, the relevant lesson is to design automation around actual loading and receiving workflows.
